column1: # 23장 말투 지시(11-10). 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명.

column2: Sunday morning in Montse's kitchen, radio off. Yuna tells Montse everything she found about the dates and the photographer, and admits she is afraid of what it means. Montse, the warm landlady who knows more than she says, listens, then gently advises her to ask her mother for the exact date. Montse speaks in the conditional ("yo en tu lugar…"), which Yuna then looks up in her grammar book. Serious and quiet.
quiet, serious
slowly, kind advice after a long silence; "yo en tu lugar" is "if I were you"
quiet, almost afraid to ask
honest and careful, a little heavy; she was wrong once before

column1: 그날 아침 나는 엄마에게 편지를 썼다
column2: plain and resolved, no more hiding
lighter, a little relieved, then restless

Tuesday in the kitchen. Montse puts two concert tickets on the table: one for Yuna, one for Marc, the reserved locksmith who walked away from Yuna after an argument on the roof a few days ago. Montse is matchmaking openly and makes a small joke that Marc's "vale" is almost a yes. She speaks to both of them with vosotros commands (Id. Escuchad.).
matter-of-fact, setting down the tickets
surprised, asking why two tickets
pleased with herself, a small joke about Marc; stress "vale"
hesitant, trailing off
warm and firm; "Id. Escuchad." as gentle orders to the two of them

Thursday evening at the Palau de la Música. Yuna meets Marc at the entrance; they are awkward and say almost nothing. Inside, the stained glass and the glass skylight amaze her. During the last, slow song Marc closes his eyes and whispers that his grandfather used to play it in the workshop. Hushed, tender, unsaid things.
quietly delighted, taking in the colors
a little shy, surprised
hushed wonder
almost a whisper, eyes closed, moved; he names the song in Catalan then in Spanish

The interval, on a small balcony over the street. Yuna tries to apologize to Marc for not telling him about her mother and the birth certificate (la partida). Marc accepts the apology but says they cannot start again until she knows the truth. Afterwards Montse waits up with warm milk. Restrained hurt on both sides, kind but distant.
nervous, unsure
hesitant, the sentence she prepared won't come out
low and calm, not cold
a sincere apology, careful; stress "debería habértelo dicho"
quietly agreeing she should have told him; not angry
searching for the word, then asking softly with hope
soft but distant, sad and honest
quiet, unfinished
calm, a promise; "Sea lo que sea" plain
flat, quietly hurt
waiting up, asking how it went
tired, a little sad
with a sigh, wry and affectionate
